We need to propose a 3-step retrosynthesis for target: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have guidance: step1: sulfonamide formation (amine + sulfonyl chloride). So retrosynthetic step: break sulfonamide to give aniline (the aryl amine) and sulfonyl chloride (Ar-SO2Cl). The target has sulfonamide linking two aromatic rings: a tolyl (para-methyl phenyl) attached to NSO2 to another phenyl bearing the unsaturated amide side chain. So disconnection: break N-S bond to give tolyl amine (p-toluidine) and sulfonyl chloride derived from the other aromatic ring (the sulfonyl chloride of 4-(... ) phenyl). So step1: sulfonamide formation.

Step2: amide formation from carboxylic acid and aniline (the second aniline). The side chain is /C=C/C(=O)N- attached to phenyl (c3ccccc3N). Actually the amide is between the unsaturated acid (cinnamic acid) and an aniline (aniline attached to phenyl). So retrosynthesis: break amide to give cinnamic acid (or its activated form) and aniline (aniline attached to phenyl). So step2: amide coupling.

Step3: Doebner modification to form the cinnamic acid from aromatic aldehyde (p-? the aromatic ring is phenyl attached to N). The side chain is attached to phenyl via N (aniline). The cinnamic acid is attached to that phenyl via the double bond: /C=C/C(=O)OH. So we need to get the aldehyde (p-? maybe 4-formyl phenyl) and malonic acid to give the cinnamic acid. So step3: Doebner modification: aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid -> alpha,beta-unsaturated carboxylic acid (cinnamic acid). So the aldehyde would be 4-aminobenzaldehyde? Wait the phenyl attached to amide nitrogen is c3ccccc3N (aniline). The amide nitrogen is attached to the phenyl ring at the para position? Actually the SMILES: ...C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N. So the amide nitrogen is attached to a phenyl that has an amino substituent (aniline). So the amide is formed between cinnamic acid and 4-aminophenyl amine (p-aminophenyl). So the amide precursor is p-aminophenyl (aniline) and cinnamic acid.

Thus step2: amide formation between cinnamic acid and p-aminophenyl (aniline). So the amide precursor is p-aminophenyl (aniline) and cinnamic acid.

Step3: cinnamic acid from p-aminobenzaldehyde (4-aminobenzaldehyde) via Doebner modification with malonic acid.

Thus overall route:

Target -> (1) sulfonamide disconnection -> p-toluidine + 4-(cinnamoylamino)phenyl sulfonyl chloride? Wait the sulfonyl chloride part includes the phenyl bearing the amide side chain. So after step1, we have p-toluidine (C c1ccc(N)cc1) and sulfonyl chloride: ClSO2-Ph- (the other phenyl) where the phenyl also has the side chain (cinnamoyl amide attached to aniline). Actually the sulfonyl chloride is attached to the phenyl that also has the amide side chain. So the sulfonyl chloride is: ClSO2-Ph- (with para substituent being the amide side chain). So we need to generate that sulfonyl chloride from the corresponding sulfonic acid or from the phenyl sulfonyl chloride precursor.

Step2: amide formation between cinnamic acid and p-aminophenyl (aniline). That yields the phenyl with amide side chain (the same phenyl as in sulfonyl chloride). So we can generate that phenyl amide first, then convert to sulfonyl chloride (by sulfonation? Actually sulfonyl chloride is attached to the phenyl via SO2Cl. To get sulfonyl chloride, we need to have the phenyl sulfonic acid then chlorinate. But we can treat as a separate step: sulfonyl chloride formation from the phenyl (maybe via chlorosulfonic acid). But the guidance only mentions sulfonamide formation, not sulfonyl chloride synthesis. So we can assume sulfonyl chloride is commercially available or can be made separately, not counted as step.

Thus we have 3 steps: (1) sulfonamide formation (target from p-toluidine + sulfonyl chloride). (2) amide formation (sulfonyl chloride precursor from cinnamic acid + p-aminophenyl). (3) Doebner modification (cinnamic acid from 4-aminobenzaldehyde + malonic acid). That's 3 steps.

Now we need to produce JSON route with nested reactions.

We need template IDs for each reaction. We have template 401931 which seems to be amide formation (carboxylic acid + amine). The retro_smarts shows amide formation from acid and amine to amide. So step2 can use template 401931.

We need a template for sulfonamide formation (amine + sulfonyl chloride). Search for template with functional_groups_formed: sulfonamides. Let's search.
